favored: large, well-capitalized banks holding government paper -- the 6M T-bill (11.90%) and 10Y PIB (12.30%) carry tailwind is intact and an 87.5%-consensus hold (zero pricing a cut) at the Sept 14 MPC keeps that carry safe; a thesis for entries on broad-tape weakness, not a chase
E&P (OGDC, PPL, MARI) benefits fundamentally from the high-oil-price backdrop, though still vulnerable to indiscriminate risk-off selling in the broader tape
avoid: OMCs -- squeezed between volatile pump prices and rising import costs amid the active oil-supply shock
autos, cement and power/IPPs -- rate-sensitive and import-cost exposed; power/IPPs carry the added overhang of unresolved circular debt heading into the IMF's still-unscheduled September review

small/thinly-capitalized banks and high-leverage rate-sensitive names -- the confirmed 11.1% CPI print plus a hawkish-hold-or-hike consensus at the Sept 14 MPC leaves zero near-term rate-relief thesis
broad cyclicals / index-chasing -- geo-risk radar pinned at max on conflict/escalation, energy-shock stress elevated, VIX ticking up -- not a dip to buy
